Their Learning Components ('Review the draft', 'Revise the draft by adding to or taking out ideas' vs 'Write simple sentences to express personal opinions...') are substantively complementary composition skills — sentence-level opinion writing produces text of the kind that process-writing review/revision operates on — giving genuine conceptual coherence within composing. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment rather than a same-rank buildsTowards. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated with 24 omitted items each, so absence of stronger linkage in the excerpt is not proof of absence in the full source.

judgment.rationale: Both Indicators sit at the same BASIC 3 rank (2) under Strand 1: Oral Language, so no lower-to-higher developmental ordering is available from the coordinate, and neither statement is a substantive deepening of the other. B3.1.7.1.2 (Sub-Strand 7: Listening Comprehension) asks learners to 'Recognise and relate the sequence of events in stories' (LCs: recognise/relate the sequence of events in stories), while B3.1.6.1.2 (Sub-Strand 6: Conversation) asks learners to 'Talk about events in the community' (LC tags: community, events, oral, talk). Beyond the shallow shared token 'events', there is genuine complementary oral-language coherence: both require learners to orally recount and organise happenings for an audience, one from narrative texts and one from lived community experience, so retelling story events reinforces and is reinforced by talking about community events. Evidence does not support asserting that proficiency in either is needed for success in the other (different sub-strands, different code families, different receptive/conversational emphases), so the symmetric relation is the supported judgment. Note that both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, including a merged Content Standard parent (B3.1.6.1) and a merged BASIC 3 grade organizer; this limits but does not contradict the above reading.

B2.2.7.1.1 asks learners to use illustrations, text clues and context to make predictions during reading (under content standard 'Understand and analyse texts read'), while B2.2.7.2.5 asks learners to use the visualisation strategy (forming mental images) to enhance understanding of level-appropriate texts (under 'Use knowledge skills and techniques of reading to understand and interpret texts'). judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 1 Content Standards (same statement-type grain, identical resolved coordinate rank 0), so any developmental direction would need substantive same-rank evidence. B1.4.2.1 (Strand 4: Writing / Sub-Strand 2: Penmanship) targets motor-graphic accuracy in copying and forming alphabet letters; B1.2.2.1 (Strand 2: Reading / Sub-Strand 2: Phonics) targets sound-letter correspondence and blending letters/syllables to read and write. The shared 'letters'/'write' vocabulary reflects genuine conceptual coherence — accurate letter formation and letter-sound knowledge are complementary components of early literacy encoding — but the supplied text gives no evidence that proficiency in one is what enables success in the other, and the two sit in different strands with no sequencing statement in the bounded excerpts. Complementary reinforcement without justified dependency supports a symmetric relatesTo. Evidence is limited: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 and 50 omitted items) and no Learning Components were supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both are Basic 3 Indicators (same statement-type grain, same Grade rank 2) under Strand 2: Reading, but in different sub-strands: B3.2.2.1.2 (Phonics) asks learners to use alphabetic knowledge to decode unknown words (blends, digraphs, vowel sounds, word patterns), while B3.2.6.1.1 (Vocabulary) asks learners to read level-appropriate sight words and understand and use them in meaningful complex sentences. These are complementary word-recognition/word-meaning skills that reinforce each other in reading: decoding handles unfamiliar words, sight-word reading handles automatically recognized words and extends to meaning and sentence use. The evidence shows no substantive expansion of one skill into the other, and at equal rank there is no source-backed basis for asserting that proficiency in either specifically supports success in the other, so a symmetric conceptual relation is the supported judgment rather than a developmental direction. Shared tokens ('words', 'use') and the weak shared code prefix (b3, 2) alone were not treated as progression evidence. Endpoint source evidence and one LC record are truncated, but the visible statement texts are sufficient for this symmetric judgment.

judgment.rationale: Indicator-grain pair, both resolved to BASIC 1 (rank 0) and both children of the merged Content Standard B1.2.7.2 'Use knowledge skills and techniques of reading to understand' in STRAND 2: READING / Sub-Strand 7: Comprehension. B1.2.7.2.4 concerns supported access to level-appropriate texts (LC tags: prompting, reading, support, texts); B1.2.7.2.6 concerns identifying narrative structure — beginning, middle, end (LC tags: comprehension, reading, story, structure). These are complementary comprehension behaviours that meaningfully reinforce one another: learners read or hear level-appropriate texts and analyse the narrative shape of such texts within the same standard. No substantive same-rank extension is evidenced: the developmental signals available are sibling hierarchy, weak source-code ordering (.4 vs .6), and trivial lexical/tag overlap ('and', 'reading'), and Basic 1 story-structure work is commonly conducted on narrated or read-aloud stories rather than depending on supported independent reading, so permitted buildsTowards is not justified in either direction. The coherence is pair-specific rather than generic repetition, so relatesTo (symmetric, null direction) applies. Limitations: both endpoints' source evidence excerpts are truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors carry upstream merge/code context, including duplicate extraction of the shared Content Standard.

The evidence shows exact recurrence rather than expanded capability: the indicator wording is unchanged, and the BASIC 3 source context label frames the work as 'Revise greetings for special occ...', i.e. deliberate revision/reinforcement of the same skill. The only differentiating text is at the parent Content Standard level ('Use certain culturally acceptable language' vs 'Explore using certain culturally acceptable language'), which is context, not indicator-level deepening, and parent-level differences alone do not establish a developmental dependency between these two indicators. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 1 Content Standards (same statement-type grain, same canonical coordinate rank 0) but sit in different strands: B1.5.4.1 'Apply knowledge of action words in communication' under Strand 5 Using Writing Conventions/Grammar Usage > Sub-Strand 4 Using Action Words, and B1.4.12.1 'Demonstrate Knowledge of description in writing' under Strand 4 Writing > Sub-Strand 12 Descriptive Writing. The bounded source excerpts show substantive coherence beyond shared tokens ('knowledge', 'in', 'of'): the grammar standard's indicator uses present-tense verbs 'to describe habitual actions', while the writing standard's indicator uses 'words and simple sentences to describe self', so verb/action-word control is a complementary language resource for descriptive composition. However, the evidence is same-rank with no source-backed sequencing, no Learning Components (none supplied for either SFI) and truncated source evidence (24 omitted items each), so a directional dependency is not substantiated; symmetric conceptual/skill coherence is the supported judgment. Code-prefix, page proximity and shared BASIC 1 grade ancestry were treated as nomination signals only.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 2 Content Standards (same grain, same rank 1, gap 0) but sit in different Strands: B2.5.4.1 'Apply knowledge of action words in communication' under Strand 5 Using Writing Conventions/Grammar Usage, Sub-Strand 4 Using Action Words; B2.4.10.1 'Narrate situations, express feelings and convey point of view about the real or fictional world' under Strand 4 Writing, Sub-Strand 10 Narrative Writing. There is genuine conceptual coherence: the action-word standard's row context points to using simple present tense to express habitual actions, feelings and opinions, which is the same expressive verb control drawn on when narrating situations and conveying feelings/point of view in writing. However, the evidence is grammar-convention knowledge applied alongside a composition task within the same grade, with no source-backed sequencing, no Learning Components on either endpoint (both lists empty) and substantially truncated source evidence (24 omitted items each), so a same-rank developmental dependency is not substantively established. Token/trigram overlap is trivial ('of', shared trigrams) and the shared BASIC 2 grade ancestor and 'b2' code segment alone are not semantic evidence. Symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 1 Indicators (same statement-type grain, identical coordinate rank 0) under Strand 5 'Using Writing Conventions/Grammar Usage', but in different Sub-Strands: B1.5.1.1.1 'Write capital letters correctly' sits under Sub-Strand 1 Using Capitalisation (parent CS 'Apply knowledge of capitalisation in writing'), while B1.5.10.1.1 'Identify and spell simple words correctly' sits under Sub-Strand 10 Spelling (parent CS 'Use phonics knowledge to spell words'; LCs 'Spell simple words correctly', 'Identify simple words', tagged phonics). They are coherent, mutually reinforcing written-accuracy conventions — correct letter formation/capitalisation and accurate word spelling both serve conventional written production — so substantive conceptual coherence exists. However, the only lexical link is the shared token 'correctly' (jaccard 0.11) and a weak code prefix 'b1.5', and at equal grade rank there is no source-backed evidence that proficiency in capital-letter writing conditions success in phonics-based spelling (or vice versa), so no developmental direction is asserted. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), limiting further exemplar-level evidence.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 1 Indicators (same statement-type grain, both canonical rank 0) within STRAND 2: READING but in different sub-strands: B1.2.7.1.1 'Use illustrations, text clues (title, headings) and context to make inferences and predictions' (Sub-Strand 7: Comprehension, under CS B1.2.7.1 'Understand texts read') and B1.2.3.1.1 'Use common rhyming endings to decode simple words' (Sub-Strand 3: Word Families, Rhyming Endings and Common Digraphs, under CS B1.2.3.1 'Employ knowledge of rhyming endings to enhance reading comprehension'). The source-backed framing of the decoding standard as serving reading comprehension gives genuine, pair-specific instructional coherence between word-recognition work and text-level meaning making, so this is more than generic repetition. It does not, however, establish same-rank developmental dependency: the comprehension indicator is explicitly anchored in illustrations, title/headings and context clues rather than in rhyming-ending decoding, and the decoding standard's comprehension purpose is stated at a general level rather than as extension into inference and prediction. Shared Grade/Strand ancestry, the shared 'reading' LC tag, 'to'/'use' token overlap, the weak 'b1.2' code prefix and rank proximity were treated as non-probative. Judged as complementary reinforcement without dependency: relatesTo with null direction, canonical endpoint order preserved. Confidence is moderate because both endpoints' source and LC evidence are truncated (24 omitted source evidence items each) and all supplied nodes carry upstream audit/merge context.

judgment.rationale: Same statement-type grain (both Indicators). B1.2.1.1.1 'Handle books appropriately' (BASIC 1, rank 0; Strand 2: Reading, Sub-Strand 1: Pre-Reading Activities, under B1.2.1.1 'Know how a text works for reading and writing') is an emergent print-concepts/book-handling behaviour. B2.6.1.1.1 'Read a variety of age and level-appropriate books and texts from print and non-print' (BASIC 2, rank 1; Strand 6: Extensive Reading, Sub-Strand 1: Building the Love and Culture of Reading, under B2.6.1.1 'Read widely for pleasure and to demonstrate independent reading and learning in the literary area') is about sustained independent engagement with varied texts. The two are substantively coherent and mutually reinforcing within early reading instruction: knowing how to handle and orient to books complements building a habit of reading varied print and non-print materials, so this is more than generic repetition of the token 'books'. But the evidence shows no substantive extension, deepening, or combination of the BASIC 1 capability in the BASIC 2 indicator — wide independent reading depends on decoding, fluency and comprehension capabilities that are not evidenced as growth from book handling, and the endpoints sit in different strands and sub-strands. Nomination support is limited to one shared LC/SFI token ('books'), a shared LC tag ('reading'), 'appropriate'/'books' trigram overlap, and weak local rank proximity, which permit direction but do not license a developmental claim. Symmetric relatesTo with null direction is therefore the supported judgment. Evidence depth is limited: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge/code context (including case-duplicate grade merges), which does not contradict this reading.

B2.5.9.1 'Understand simple sentences in writing' (Strand 5 Using Writing Conventions/Grammar Usage, Sub-Strand 9 Using Simple and Compound Sentences; bounded indicator 'Identify the structure of simple sentences') addresses sentence-internal grammatical structure, while B2.4.7.2 'Matching parts of sentences to composition' (Strand 4 Writing, Sub-Strand 7 Controlled Writing; bounded indicator 'Re-arrange jumbled sentences logically' within a retold story) addresses assembling and ordering sentences into a coherent composition. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 1 Indicators (same grade rank 0), so no rank-based developmental direction applies, and neither statement shows substantive expansion of the other. Evidence is mainly thin token overlap ('stories') plus a shared grade ancestor, which alone would not suffice; the pair-specific narrative-understanding coherence supports symmetric relatesTo only. Their source rows show parallel oral-performance work (listening to and singing familiar songs; listening to and reciting rhymes and tongue-twisters with actions), so they are substantively coherent complementary oral-language experiences that mutually reinforce listening, expression and appreciation of oral/literary forms. There is no evidence that proficiency with songs is needed for, or expands into, appreciating literary pieces: they are same-grade parallel sub-strands, and the shared tokens ('a', 'of', 'variety'), shared code prefix and same source page are weak, non-developmental signals. Same-rank placement with no substantive expansion of capability therefore supports symmetric relatesTo rather than a direction. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so deeper indicator-level evidence was not available; this does not alter the parallel, non-dependent reading.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 3 Indicators (same statement-type grain, identical coordinate rank 2, gap 0) grounded in phonics. B3.2.5.1.1 'Use consonant blends to build words' sits under Strand 2 Reading / Sub-Strand 5 Blends and Consonant Clusters, while B3.4.3.1.1 'Use letter-sound relationships to represent most letters in words correctly' sits under Strand 4 Writing / Sub-Strand 3 Writing-Copying Letters, with parent standard B3.4.3.1 explicitly invoking 'knowledge of letter-sounds'. LC tags confirm shared 'phonics' (consonant blends/word building vs letter-sound/spelling/writing). This is substantive complementary coherence — applying sound-symbol knowledge to build words in reading and to represent letters in written words — but neither source text nor the same-rank coordinates supply evidence that proficiency in one is developmentally required for or clearly supportive of the other in a specific direction; the different strands/sub-strands are parallel applications rather than a sequence. Shared Grade ancestor and the weak 'b3' code-prefix overlap are not by themselves relational evidence. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), so exemplar-level detail that might establish direction is unavailable.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 1 Indicators (rank 0, same Grade coordinate) in STRAND 2: READING, but in different sub-strands: B1.2.7.2.5 sits under Sub-Strand 7 Comprehension ('Use a variety of comprehension-strategies e.g. prediction before reading a text, cover page') while B1.2.3.1.1 sits under Sub-Strand 3 Word Families, Rhyming Endings and Common Digraphs ('Use common rhyming endings to decode simple words'). Their content is coherent rather than dependent: the second indicator's parent Content Standard explicitly frames rhyming-ending knowledge as 'to enhance reading comprehension', so word-level decoding and text-level comprehension strategies are complementary reading capabilities that reinforce one another. However, the specific first indicator concerns pre-reading prediction cues (cover page, prediction before reading), which does not require decoding proficiency, and vice versa, so no same-rank developmental direction is substantively supported; the nomination's lexical evidence is weak (single shared token 'use', jaccard ~0.05, one shared LC tag 'reading') and shared Grade/Strand ancestry alone is not a semantic verdict. relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment. Note both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence; omitted excerpts could contain further detail not visible here.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 2 Indicators (rank 1, same Grade coordinate) under the same Content Standard B2.2.7.2 ('Use knowledge skills and techniques of reading to understand and interpret texts') in Strand 2: Reading / Sub-Strand 7: Comprehension. B2.2.7.2.1 targets understanding the purpose and features of information texts (text-type/genre awareness), while B2.2.7.2.5 targets a specific comprehension strategy (visualisation, forming mental images) to enhance understanding of level-appropriate texts. They share the 'comprehension' LC tag and a common goal of text understanding, giving substantive conceptual coherence, but neither is a stated or implied precondition for the other: genre-feature knowledge and strategy use are complementary sub-skills taught at the same grade level, and the only ordering evidence is adjacent indicator numbering, which is not developmental evidence. Same-rank direction lacks substantive support, so the symmetric relation is chosen. Evidence limits: pair nomination evidence and both endpoints' source evidence are truncated, and the second endpoint's LC evidence is truncated, so unseen exemplars could alter the reading; the retained conceptual overlap is nonetheless sufficient for relatesTo.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 1 Indicators (rank 0, same coordinate) sharing the single parent Content Standard B1.2.7.2 'Use knowledge skills and techniques of reading to understand' within STRAND 2: READING / Sub-Strand 7: Comprehension. B1.2.7.2.3 asks learners to connect ideas and information in stories to their own experiences and knowledge of the world; B1.2.7.2.5 asks learners to use a variety of comprehension strategies such as prediction before reading, using the cover page. These are substantively coherent, complementary comprehension behaviours (activating prior knowledge is conceptually allied to pre-reading prediction), and the LC tags overlap on 'comprehension' and 'reading'. However, neither statement subsumes, extends, or presupposes the other: strategy use and text-to-self connection are parallel indicators at the same grade rank, and with identical rank the evidence does not substantively justify a developmental direction (code-order, page proximity and shared parent are not semantic progression evidence). Endpoint source evidence is truncated and the nomination evidence is truncated, so only the bounded excerpts were used; they suffice for symmetric coherence but not for dependency.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 3 (rank 2) Indicators realising the same Content Standard B3.2.7.2, 'Use knowledge, skills and techniques of reading to understand, interpret and appreciate a variety of literary texts', within Strand 2: Reading / Sub-Strand 7: Comprehension. B3.2.7.2.1 concerns demonstrating understanding of the purpose and features of literary forms (poems or rhymes, fables), split into two Learning Components for 'purpose' and 'features'; B3.2.7.2.2 concerns responding to stories with one's own opinion and value judgment. These are complementary comprehension-and-appreciation capabilities applied to literary texts, giving pair-specific instructional coherence beyond generic repetition, so relatesTo is warranted. A directional buildsTowards is not supported: both sit at the same canonical rank, and the only directional signals available are sibling code adjacency (B3.2.7.2.1 vs B3.2.7.2.2), shared parentage, identical source page/table row, and a single shared token ('and', jaccard 0.05), none of which count as semantic evidence. The text types also differ (poems/rhymes/fables vs stories), so proficiency in describing the purpose and features of poems and fables is not shown to raise the likelihood of success in forming and justifying opinions and value judgments about stories. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry upstream audit/merge context, which caps confidence.

First SFI B1.1.9.1.2 'Make and respond to polite requests using the word "Please"' (LCs: make polite requests; respond to polite requests) and second SFI B1.1.9.1.1 'Give and respond to commands and instructions' (LCs: give commands and instructions; respond to commands and instructions) are complementary oral directive speech acts sharing the same production-plus-response structure, so they reinforce each other in a specific, useful instructional way rather than by generic repetition. No developmental dependency is supported: the parent standard lists commands, instructions, directions and requests as coordinate categories, so these indicators are parallel decomposition of one standard; hasChild decomposition, the .1/.2 code order, source-page proximity, weak local_rank_proximity (rank_gap 0), and shared surface tokens ('and', 'respond', 'to') are non-semantic. Adding the politeness marker 'Please' is a lateral register/pragmatic variant, not demonstrated increased complexity, and same-rank buildsTowards requires substantive extension evidence that the bounded excerpt does not supply. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment, with canonical endpoint order preserved and direction null. Truncated source evidence on both endpoints and truncated nomination evidence limit certainty; ancestor merge context (CONT'D standard row merge; case-variant Grade merge) was considered and does not change the reading.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 3 Indicators under Strand 2: Reading (rank 2 for both), but in different sub-strands: 'Use consonant blends to build words' (B3.2.5.1.1, Sub-Strand 5: Blends and Consonant Clusters, under standard 'Identify and use consonant blends in words') and 'Use basic elements of structural analysis (e.g prefixes, suffixes, compound, root words) to decode unknown words' (B3.2.2.1.3, Sub-Strand 2: Phonics, under 'Connect sounds to letters and blend letters/syllables in order to read and write'). They are coherent, complementary word-level skills: one manipulates sound-level consonant clusters to construct words, the other analyses morphological units to decode unfamiliar words, and both LCs share the 'phonics' tag. The evidence shows no substantive deepening or extension of one into the other at the same grade rank — the units of analysis (phonemes/blends vs. morphemes) differ rather than nest — so a same-rank developmental direction is not warranted; meaningful reinforcement within Basic 3 word-recognition work supports relatesTo. Shared Strand/Grade ancestry, weak code-prefix overlap ('b3','2'), and page proximity alone were not treated as semantic evidence, and the generic token overlap ('to','use','words') was discounted. Noted limitations: source evidence for both endpoints and the second endpoint's LC metadata are truncated, so the full exemplar text is not available.

The shared evidence is substantive rather than merely lexical: wide independent reading of level-appropriate texts and strategic comprehension of such texts mutually reinforce each other, and the LC tags ('reading','texts' vs 'comprehension','visualisation','reading') show complementary rather than nested skills. At equal grade rank there is no substantive evidence that proficiency in either is a developmental support for the other (extensive reading volume and a taught comprehension strategy are parallel, concurrently taught capabilities), so a directional buildsTowards is not warranted. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 1 Indicators (resolved Grade coordinates, rank 0 each) in STRAND 2: READING. The first (B1.2.9.1.2, Sub-Strand 9: Fluency, under 'Read texts with good speed, accuracy and expression') requires automatic recognition of one hundred and twenty printed sight words including content words; its LC is 'Recognise one hundred and twenty sight words including content words'. The second (B1.2.1.2.1, Sub-Strand 1: Pre-Reading Activities, under 'Manipulate the sounds of the letters of English') requires orally blending two or three sounds into a one-syllable word (a-sh = ash); its LC is 'Blend sounds to produce simple syllables/words'. These are complementary word-level reading capabilities within the same grade and strand — assembling spoken words from component sounds and recognising whole printed words at speed — giving substantive, pair-specific instructional coherence rather than mere repeated wording. However, the evidence does not establish that proficiency in oral blending expands into or supports the sight-word bank: they sit in separate Sub-Strands with no sequencing signal, they are at the same rank (rank_gap 0), and sight-word work is explicitly automatic whole-word recognition rather than sound-by-sound decoding. The nomination signals are weak (shared tokens 'one'/'words', jaccard 0.03-0.07, weak code prefix 'b1.2', shared Grade/Strand ancestors), and shared hierarchy or wording alone cannot license a developmental direction. Symmetric relatesTo with null direction is therefore the supported judgment. Truncated source evidence for both endpoints and truncated LC evidence for eb456d2d limit deeper corroboration, and merge/audit context on several ancestors (including the merged BASIC 1 grade node and merged Content Standard B1.2.1.2) remains unresolved upstream.

judgment.rationale: B1.4.5.1.1 'Make a list of objects in the school' (BASIC 1, STRAND 4: WRITING, Sub-Strand 5: Writing Simple Words and Sentences, CS B1.4.5.1 'Write words and sentences') and B1.4.4.1.1 'Draw simple pictures of peers or various objects and use invented spelling to write about oneself' (BASIC 1, same Strand, Sub-Strand 4: Labelling Items, CS B1.4.4.1 'Draw and label simple objects') are same-grain Indicators at the same resolved coordinate (rank 0). They cohere substantively: both are early written-production tasks in the Writing strand in which learners commit words to paper in relation to concrete objects in their environment (LCs: 'make a list of objects in the school'; 'draw simple pictures of peers or various objects'; 'use invented spelling to write about oneself'). This is complementary, mutually reinforcing emergent-writing work, not mere repetition of wording. It does not, however, support a directional developmental claim: at equal rank, the second endpoint's actual writing demand is invented-spelling composition about oneself rather than labelling or listing object names, and the evidence does not show that listing objects is a substantive extension of it (nor the reverse). Code ordering (B1.4.4 before B1.4.5), adjacent page indexes, zero rank gap, and shared 'objects'/'writing' tokens are non-semantic signals and cannot establish direction. Hence symmetric relatesTo in canonical endpoint order with null direction. Limitations: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each, one excerpt cut mid-record) and both endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, which is retained rather than resolved.

producer_judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 1 Indicators (rank 0, same canonical Grade coordinate) under STRAND 4: WRITING, so direction rests on substantive content rather than rank. B1.4.4.1.1 (Sub-Strand 4: Labelling Items, under Content Standard 'Draw and label simple objects') has learners draw pictures of peers/objects and use invented spelling to write about themselves — emergent, heavily scaffolded word-level writing about objects. B1.4.5.1.1 (Sub-Strand 5: Writing Simple Words and Sentences, under 'Write words and sentences') requires producing a written list of objects in the school without a drawing scaffold, i.e. independent word writing in a purposeful list form. Proficiency with labelling/invented-spelling writing of object names plausibly supports success in composing a written list of object names, so the developmental support runs from the second SFI to the first. Same-grade recurrence of 'objects'/'writing' alone would not suffice; the judgment rests on the shift from drawing-supported invented spelling to unaided word/list writing. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and one excerpt is cut mid-record, so exemplar detail beyond the indicator text is unavailable.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 2 Indicators (rank 1, same coordinate) under the identical Content Standard B2.1.9.1 'Demonstrate understanding in commands, instructions, directions and requests' within Oral Language Sub-Strand 9. This is substantive complementary coherence within one standard rather than evidence that proficiency in one supports success in the other; at equal grade rank the only directional signal is the adjacent code sequence (.2 before .3), which is weak and not semantically decisive, so a symmetric relation is preferred over an unsupported developmental direction. They are complementary writing capabilities — a composed persuasive paragraph is exactly the kind of own writing that can be read aloud and published — giving substantive coherence, but at the same grade rank there is no evidence that proficiency in one supports success in the other: reading aloud is a generic publishing routine, not a dependency for constructing reasoned argument, and vice versa. judgment.rationale: Same-grain Indicator pair, both BASIC 1 (rank 0, resolved Grade coordinates) under STRAND 2: READING but in different Sub-Strands. B1.2.9.1.2 (Sub-Strand 9: Fluency, parent Content Standard 'Read texts with good speed, accuracy and expression') asks learners to recognise one hundred and twenty sight words including content words. B1.2.6.1.1 (Sub-Strand 6: Vocabulary, parent 'Understand word meanings and usages') asks learners to read level-appropriate sight words and use many of them in meaningful sentences, with LCs 'Read level-appropriate sight words' and 'Use many sight words in meaningful sentences'. These are substantively complementary sight-word capabilities within the same grade: automatic recognition of a defined sight-word corpus for fluent text reading alongside reading and productive sentence-level use of sight words for meaning. That is pair-specific instructional coherence rather than generic repeated wording, so no_relation is not warranted. A directional claim is not supported: the vocabulary indicator itself includes a reading/recognition component at least as foundational as the fluency corpus target, so first_to_second and second_to_first are equally arguable on this evidence, and same-rank (gap 0) development requires substantive one-directional evidence that the excerpts do not provide. The nomination signals (shared Grade/Strand ancestors, 'sight words' token/trigram overlap, weak 'b1.2' code prefix, weak rank proximity) are not by themselves semantic direction evidence. Judged as symmetric relatesTo in canonical endpoint order. Their LCs share the 'phonics' tag and both operate on building/spelling words, so they are substantively coherent complementary encoding and decoding/word-building skills that reinforce each other. However, the evidence does not support a developmental dependency in either direction at the same grade rank: diphthong word-building concerns regular vowel-pattern words, whereas the spelling indicator targets phonically *irregular* words, which are explicitly exceptions to such patterns. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment; both endpoints' source evidence is truncated, which limits deeper exemplar-level comparison.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 2 Content Standards (rank 1, no grade gap) under the same Strand 1: Oral Language but different sub-strands: B2.1.4.1 'Respond to stories' (Sub-Strand 4: Story Telling) and B2.1.2.1 'Show understanding of a variety of literary pieces' (Sub-Strand 2: Rhymes, whose indicator context concerns interpreting rhymes and tongue-twisters in own words). They share substantive coherence as oral-language comprehension and response to spoken literary forms, so the skills meaningfully reinforce each other. However, neither statement's bounded evidence shows one being a deepening, extension, or enabling capability for the other at the same grade rank: responding to stories and interpreting rhymes/tongue-twisters are parallel applications in distinct sub-strands, and the nomination signals (shared ancestors, adjacent pages, one shared trigram 'rie', weak 'b2.1' code prefix) are not semantic developmental evidence. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment. Note both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and neither carries Learning Components, so any finer-grained dependency could not be assessed.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 3 Indicators (same rank 2, same statement grain) under Strand 4: Writing, but in different sub-strands: B3.4.9.3.1 'Review and revise the draft, adding to or taking out ideas' sits under Sub-Strand 9 'Writing as a Process' / CS B3.4.9.3 (apply strategies for improving drafts for publishing), while B3.4.5.1.3 'Draw pictures and write, at least, three sentences to share an opinion' sits under Sub-Strand 5 'Writing Simple Words and Sentences' / CS B3.4.5.1 (write accurately using vocabulary and grammar). Their LCs ('revise the draft by adding to or taking out ideas', 'review the draft' vs 'write, at least, three sentences to share an opinion', 'draw pictures to share an opinion') show substantive coherence: composing short opinion text and reviewing/revising drafted ideas are complementary composition skills that reinforce one another within the same grade's writing work. The evidence does not, however, establish a same-rank developmental dependency in either direction; the nomination signals (shared Strand/Grade ancestors, shared 'b3'/'4' code segments, token overlap limited to 'and'/'to') are structural rather than semantic, so relatesTo rather than buildsTowards is warranted. Note both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and the second endpoint's LC evidence is truncated, and several endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context (including the merged BASIC 3 grade organizer and the merged continued CS B3.4.5.1), which bounds but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 3 Indicators (same statement-type grain, rank 2, rank gap 0) under Strand 1: Oral Language, but in different Sub-Strands and under different Content Standards: B3.1.4.1.3 'Create own events to extend stories heard' (Sub-Strand 4: Story Telling, under 'Respond to stories') and B3.1.7.1.3 'Share facts from information texts heard with a partner, groups or the teacher' (Sub-Strand 7: Listening Comprehension, under 'Use appropriate skills and strategies to process meaning from texts'). They share substantive coherence as complementary oral-language responses to material heard: each requires attentive listening and then an oral production drawn from that text. However, the demands differ in kind rather than in depth — imaginative narrative extension of a story versus accurate factual recall and sharing from an information text — so neither reliably underwrites the other and no developmental direction is supported at the same grade rank; the token/trigram overlap is only the shared word 'heard' and a weak shared code prefix, which alone carry no semantic weight. relatesTo captures the meaningful reinforcement without asserting dependency.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 3 Indicators (same grain, identical rank 2 coordinate). B3.4.3.1.1 sits under Strand 4: Writing / Sub-Strand 3: Writing/Copying Letters and asks learners to use letter-sound relationships to represent most letters in words correctly; B3.2.2.1.3 sits under Strand 2: Reading / Sub-Strand 2: Phonics and asks learners to use structural analysis (prefixes, suffixes, compound, root words) to decode unknown words. They share a word-level phonics/word-analysis focus (LC tag overlap 'phonics'; encoding words versus decoding words) and reinforce each other across the writing and reading strands, but neither is a sound-to-symbol precondition for morphological structural analysis: one operates at grapheme-phoneme encoding for spelling, the other at morpheme-level decoding. With identical grade rank and no source evidence of increased complexity or dependency between them, a directional buildsTowards is not supported; substantive complementary coherence supports relatesTo. Both endpoints' source evidence excerpts are truncated and the second endpoint's LC evidence is truncated, so only the bounded statement text and hierarchy were used.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators (same statement-type grain) within the identically titled Sub-Strand 'Word Families-Rhyming Endings and Common Digraphs' under Strand 2: Reading, each under a near-identical Content Standard about employing rhyming endings and common digraphs for reading comprehension (B2.2.3.1 / B3.2.3.1). The indicator texts are verbatim identical ('Use words containing digraphs to make meaningful sentences'), and they share the single Learning Component fade127a with identical skill text and tags — strong, pair-specific instructional coherence about using digraph-containing words in sentence construction, so this is not generic unrelated repetition. However, the bounded evidence shows no textual or component-level expansion at BASIC 3 (rank 2) relative to BASIC 2 (rank 1): no broadened word set, added complexity, or new task demand is stated. Per the curriculum policy, progression must not be inferred from repeated wording alone, so this is meaningful cross-grade reinforcement of the same skill rather than an evidenced developmental step; relatesTo is recorded instead of buildsTowards. Source evidence and LC metadata for both endpoints are truncated, so an expansion present in the full source cannot be ruled out.

judgment.rationale: B2.4.7.1 'Write simple compositions' (Sub-Strand 7: Controlled Writing) and B2.4.2.1 'Copy and rewrite sentences correctly' (Sub-Strand 2: Penmanship/Handwriting) are both BASIC 2 Content Standards under STRAND 4: WRITING with resolved coordinates at the same rank (1). Beyond shared ancestry and the weak structural triggers (rank gap 0 'weak', code prefix 'b2'/'4' 'weak', trigram Jaccard 0.098), the bounded source_context_labels show pair-specific instructional coherence: the composition standard's indicator is 'Write or copy correct sentences from substitution tables', and the penmanship standard's indicator is 'Copy sentences clearly ... practise writing legibly'. Accurate, legible sentence production and controlled composition of simple texts are complementary same-grade writing capabilities that meaningfully reinforce one another, but the evidence does not show that either standard substantively extends or enables the other, and same-rank buildsTowards requires such substantive evidence; the composition standard carries its own copying activity rather than depending on the handwriting standard. Therefore canonical symmetric relatesTo with null direction. Judgment rests on truncated endpoint evidence (24 omitted source-evidence items each) and endpoints/ancestors carrying upstream audit/merge/code context.

The shared tokens are only 'in'/'writing', but the substantive coherence is real: mechanical conventions (capital letters for initials and abbreviations, per the source row excerpt) are applied within the composed paragraphs in which pupils state and support an opinion, so the two standards mutually reinforce one composition practice. There is no evidence of dependency or sequence between them — they are parallel same-grade standards in distinct strands, one addressing composition/idea development and the other surface conventions — so a same-rank developmental direction is not substantiated and relatesTo is the supported judgment. Evidence is bounded: both endpoints carry truncated source evidence (24 omitted items each) and no Learning Components were supplied, so finer-grained exemplar alignment could not be checked.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 1 Indicators (same statement-type grain, identical coordinate rank 0) centred on the letters of the alphabet: B1.2.2.1.1 'Identify the alphabet in order' sits under Strand 2 Reading / Sub-Strand Phonics (Content Standard B1.2.2.1, connecting sounds to letters), while B1.4.2.1.1 'Copy letters of the alphabet clearly' sits under Strand 4 Writing / Sub-Strand Penmanship (Content Standard B1.4.2.1, copy and write letters correctly). Their Learning Components share the tags 'alphabet' and 'letters', giving genuine conceptual coherence between alphabet recognition and alphabet formation. However, the copying indicator is a handwriting/motor task framed around lines, spaces and letter formation rather than a task whose success is asserted to depend on ordered alphabet identification, and both sit at the same grade rank with no source evidence of sequencing between the Reading and Writing strands; same-rank developmental direction is therefore not substantively supported. Symmetric relatesTo is the appropriate judgment. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so absence of an explicit cross-strand link in the excerpts is not proof of absence in the full source.

Symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment.

B3.2.7.2.3 asks learners to use the visualisation strategy (forming mental images while reading) to enhance understanding of level-appropriate texts; B3.2.7.2.4 asks learners to read level-appropriate texts independently. These are complementary comprehension expectations addressed to the same text level and the same reading purpose: one names a strategy for building understanding, the other the autonomous reading context in which such strategies are exercised. That is substantive, pair-specific instructional coherence rather than mere repeated wording, so relatesTo is warranted. A same-rank buildsTowards is not supported: the two indicators are co-listed parallel expectations in the same source table row, and the only directional signals available are weak or non-semantic (sequential code order .3 then .4, 'level-appropriate texts' token/trigram overlap, page proximity, shared ancestors, shared LC tags 'reading'/'comprehension'). No evidence shows that independent reading deepens, extends, or combines the visualisation strategy specifically, and the generic claim that a comprehension strategy aids independent reading would apply to every indicator in this sub-strand. Confidence is moderated because the pair's nomination evidence and both endpoints' source/LC evidence are truncated, and all endpoint ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context (including merged Strand and Grade organizers) that has been preserved rather than resolved.

The pair shows meaningful, pair-specific instructional coherence beyond shared words: controlling the simple present tense to express feelings, interests and opinions is the grammatical counterpart to composing simple written sentences that express feelings, so the two indicators reinforce one another as complementary skills within the same grade. The nomination signals (shared Strand/Grade ancestry, weak 'b3.4' code-prefix overlap, single shared token 'the', low-jaccard trigram overlap) are structural/lexical only and cannot establish dependency or sequence. The first (B1.2.2.1.5, Sub-Strand 2 Phonics, under B1.2.2.1 'Connect sounds to letters and blend letters/syllables in order to read and write') requires segmenting syllables/words into their constituent sounds; the second (B1.2.1.2.1, Sub-Strand 1 Pre-Reading Activities, under B1.2.1.2 'Manipulate the sounds of the letters of English') requires orally blending two or three sounds into a one-syllable word with worked exemplars (a-sh = ash). Learning Components confirm the shared sound/syllable construct ('Segment syllables/words into sounds' vs 'Blend sounds to produce simple syllables/words'), giving genuine pair-specific instructional coherence beyond shared wording: they are the two converse operations on the same phonological unit and are routinely taught as mutually reinforcing partners. However, the evidence does not show one expanding, deepening, or combining the other: the operations are inverse rather than cumulative, both sit at the same BASIC 1 rank (so a directional claim needs substantive same-rank evidence), and the only ordering signals are code sequence and sub-strand position, which are not semantic. Supplied LC metadata also shows a separate oral-segmenting indicator (8985c25e...) in the Pre-Reading sub-strand that aggregates into the same segmenting LC, indicating the curriculum provides oral counterparts of both operations and undercutting a specific blending-to-segmenting dependency. Accordingly this is symmetric relatesTo with null direction. Evidence limitation: both endpoints have 24 omitted source-evidence items and truncated LC metadata, and several ancestors carry merge/CONT'D audit context, so the judgment rests on the bounded statement text, sub-strand placement, and LC descriptions.

B2.2.2.1 (Strand 2 Reading / Sub-Strand 2 Phonics) asks learners to 'Connect sounds to letters and blend letters/syllables in order to read and write'; B2.4.5.1 (Strand 4 Writing / Sub-Strand 5 Writing Simple Words and Sentences) asks learners to 'Use knowledge of grammar and vocabulary to write words and sentences correctly.' The phonics statement's own purpose clause names writing as an application, and the writing sub-strand is about producing simple words and sentences, so there is genuine, pair-specific instructional coherence: sound-letter and blending work and the production of correct written words and sentences are complementary literacy skills taught in the same year. However, the target standard's capability is explicitly grounded in grammar and vocabulary knowledge, not in orthographic encoding or spelling, and no Learning Components are supplied for either endpoint to bridge phonics to that grammar/vocabulary base. Proficiency in connecting sounds to letters therefore is not shown to support success in the specific capability B2.4.5.1 names, so a developmental buildsTowards is not justified; the relationship is symmetric conceptual coherence. This goes beyond generic repetition or the weak structural signals in the nomination (shared BASIC 2 Grade ancestor at distance 3, shared 'b2' code segment, weak local-rank proximity, token jaccard 0.16 on 'and'/'to'/'write'), so no_relation is too strong, and the evidence is consistent rather than contradictory, so needs_review is unnecessary. judgment.rationale: Same-grain Content Standards at the same resolved Grade coordinate (BASIC 2, rank 1, gap 0) in different strands: B2.6.1.1 'Read widely for pleasure and to demonstrate independent reading and learning in the literary area' (Strand 6 Extensive Reading / Sub-Strand 1) and B2.2.9.1 'Read texts fluently' (Strand 2 Reading / Sub-Strand 9 Fluency). The visible statement text and excerpt context (fluent reading of texts with good pace, accuracy and expression; reading a variety of age- and level-appropriate books) show genuine, pair-specific reading coherence: these are complementary same-grade reading capabilities that mutually reinforce learners' engagement with connected text, which is more than the weak nomination signals (shared Grade ancestor, rank proximity, single shared token 'read', 'b2' code prefix). However, the evidence does not position either standard as a deepening, extension, or enabling stage of the other: they are concurrently taught parallel strands at identical rank, and same-rank developmental direction requires substantive pair-specific evidence that is absent. Therefore canonical relatesTo with null direction, endpoint order unchanged. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so this judgment rests on the visible statement text, hierarchy, and excerpt context; upstream audit/merge/code-context warnings for both endpoints and their ancestors are retained and unresolved.

producer_judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 2 Content Standards (same statement-type grain, same resolved Grade rank 1), but they sit in different Strand/Sub-Strand contexts: B2.2.9.1 'Read texts fluently' under Strand 2: Reading / Sub-Strand 9: Fluency, and B2.6.1.1 'Read widely for pleasure and to demonstrate independent reading and learning in the literary area' under Strand 6: Extensive Reading / Sub-Strand 1: Building the Love and Culture of Reading. The source context shows the fluency standard focuses on reading texts with good pace, accuracy and expression, which is the enabling component skill for the extensive-reading standard's demand for wide, independent, self-sustained reading of age- and level-appropriate books. Proficiency in fluent text reading therefore supports likelihood of success in sustained independent wide reading, justifying a same-rank developmental direction from the fluency standard (second) to the extensive-reading standard (first) rather than mere shared vocabulary ('read'), shared BASIC 2 grade ancestor, or the weak 'b2' code-prefix overlap that triggered nomination. Both endpoints' source evidence excerpts are truncated with 24 omitted source-evidence items each, so the judgment rests on the visible statement text and hierarchy; direction is asserted as supportive, not as a mandatory prerequisite or teaching sequence.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 1 (rank 0) Indicators within STRAND 2: READING / Sub-Strand 7: Comprehension, so same-grain Indicator comparison applies. B1.2.7.1.2 asks learners to ask and answer factual, inferential and applicative questions about level-appropriate texts (LCs tagged ask/answer, questions, texts, comprehension), while B1.2.7.2.6 asks learners to identify story structure (beginning, middle, end) under a different Content Standard (B1.2.7.2 'Use knowledge skills and techniques of reading to understand'). These are complementary comprehension capabilities that mutually reinforce text understanding, but the evidence shows no substantive same-rank developmental dependency in either direction: questioning about texts is not a stated precondition for recognising narrative structure, nor conversely. Shared ancestry, shared 'comprehension' LC tag, code prefix b1.2.7 and 'and' token overlap are not by themselves progression evidence, so relatesTo rather than buildsTowards is warranted. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), limiting exemplar-level detail, but the available statement text is sufficient for a symmetric coherence judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 2 Indicators (same rank 1) in Strand 1: Oral Language, Sub-Strand 6 (Conversation and Talking about Oneself, Family, ... Events ...), but sit under different Content Standards: B2.1.6.2.1 'Demonstrate turn-taking in conversations' (under B2.1.6.2, applying language and communicative skills to participate in conversation) and B2.1.6.1.2 'Talk about events at home' (under B2.1.6.1, using culturally acceptable language for communication). Same-grade placement means a developmental direction would require substantive evidence of expanded capability; here the two describe complementary facets of the same conversational competence — interactional mechanics (turn-taking) versus topic-based personal talk about home events — with neither text indicating that one is presupposed by or extends the other. Shared LC tokens ('oral language') plus shared page/code prefix are weak organizational signals only, so symmetric conceptual coherence within the Conversation sub-strand is the supported judgment.

Neither statement's text or Learning Components ('match parts of sentences to compose meaningful texts' vs 'capitalise titles of texts', 'use capital letters at the beginning of names of people') indicates that one capability is presupposed by or extends the other; the nomination signals (shared BASIC 1 grade ancestor, adjacent pages 54/55, shared 'b1' code prefix, token overlaps limited to 'of', 'texts', 'writing') are weak and not themselves semantic. However, there is genuine instructional coherence within Basic 1 written production: composing meaningful sentence-level texts and correctly capitalising titles and names of people are complementary components of producing conventionally correct written text, so symmetric relatesTo is supported rather than a direction. Evidence is bounded: source evidence and supporting LC evidence are truncated for both endpoints (24 omitted source evidence items each), so exemplar-level linkage cannot be confirmed or ruled out.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 3 (rank 2) Indicators under Strand 2: Reading, so the rank gap is 0 and buildsTowards would need substantive same-rank developmental evidence. B3.2.3.1.1 'Use common rhyming/endings words for decoding of words' (Sub-Strand 3: Word Families, Rhyming Endings and Common Digraphs; parent CS B3.2.3.1 'Employ knowledge of rhyming endings and common digraphs to enhance reading comprehension'; LC tags decoding, rhyming, word families) is a word-recognition skill. B3.2.7.2.3 'Use visualisation strategy (form mental images when reading text) to enhance understanding of level-appropriate texts' (Sub-Strand 7: Comprehension; parent CS B3.2.7.2 on using reading knowledge/skills to understand and interpret texts; LC tags comprehension, mental images, visualisation) is a text-level meaning-construction strategy. Visualisation is not a deepening, extension, or combination of decoding common rhyming/ending words; the only link offered is the generic proposition that decoding supports reading comprehension, which is not pair-specific curricular evidence and cannot license same-grade development. There is nonetheless real instructional coherence: within the same Basic 3 Reading strand the curriculum pairs word-recognition skill (explicitly framed as serving reading comprehension) with an explicit comprehension strategy applied to level-appropriate texts, making them complementary reinforcing skills without dependency or sequence. Nomination signals are non-probative here (shared Strand/Grade ancestors, weak code-prefix segments 'b3'/'2', token overlap only on 'of'/'use', weak zero-gap rank proximity). Limitations retained: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), the second endpoint's LC metadata is truncated, and several ancestors/endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context that was not independently resolvable.
